title: Spec 256 FR-004 ('every record') contradicts Decision 2 ('any record') on clearing revision free text
intended: Decision 2 / ADR-0013 (accepted): clear free text when any record of the revision is redacted (HD-1302 supported).
observed: Implementation and live behaviour follow 'any' (fresh: upstream spanning-revision test in the original run; intent lane B record HD-1302). The spec's FR-004 wording is stale.
remedy: Edit FR-004 to say 'any record', matching Decision 2 and ADR-0013.
notes: Documentation conflict; product behaviour matches the accepted decision.

title: Redaction can tombstone history of content a concurrent commit made live (unlocked start, late marker)
intended: RED-B1.1 / ADR-0013: a redaction never tombstones live content; the marker refuses commits into the target from the start.
observed: Original live reproduction on the same pin (scenario commit_in_unmarked_window, which compiles the original probe class and is not rerun here) and as-built model trace (3 steps); the opening checks run without the head lock and the marker is set at the first tombstone (LedgerRedact.cls:202-211, 322-324). Fresh model and proof evidence: core lanes (pending).
remedy: Check liveness and set the marker in one transaction under the head lock (HD-1301 working answer).
notes: Original evidence attributable to submission 9c3719c1 at the same product pin.

title: Concurrent redactions of two targets mix their audit counts and one removes the other's marker
intended: Decision 1: each redaction revision records what it redacted; one target at a time (RED-B6, RED-B7.1).
observed: Fresh rerun on the pin: both runs pass the 'another redaction?' check, each target gets a redaction revision, and the audits' record counts are mixed (shared counters; Final reads them under any marker, LedgerRedact.cls:409-462).
remedy: Own the marker per target from the start and let Batch/Final act only under their own marker; keep counters per target.

title: An unprefixed default-graph redaction tombstones history of nodes live in a named graph
intended: RED-X2 / FR-005: never redact content that is live in any graph; HD-1303(b) working answer: refuse an ambiguous unprefixed default-graph target unless no matching node is live anywhere.
observed: Fresh rerun: redact(None) is accepted although tenant B's nodes are live in a named graph, tombstones their node records (graph-blind), and verify then diverges. Independently reproduced by intent lane B.
remedy: Count live nodes in every graph for an unprefixed default-graph target (as LiveRows already does for prefixed ones), or refuse it.
notes: Three targeting predicates differ (Matches, LiveRows, DropStatements); see the core models.

title: A graph-per-tenant redaction with unprefixed ids reports success while the tenant's node history remains
intended: Spec 256: tenant erasure removes the tenant's content from history (RED-B1.2, SC-001).
observed: Fresh rerun: redact(gTenantA) completes; tenant A's node ids and property values stay in the ledger (node records are graph-blind); verify diverges.
remedy: Return an explicit incomplete/refused outcome when node history cannot be attributed (HD-1304 working answer), or record each node record's graph.

title: A retried commit re-applies post-commit properties and revives erased content
intended: HD-1305 (supported): a retry must not recreate an erased tenant's properties; idempotency contract.
observed: Fresh rerun: the replay of a retried commit re-applies the post-commit property; an erased node's property is live again. Intent lane B additionally observed the property write landing in a target while its redaction marker was set (RED-B5 bypass).
remedy: Do not reapply post-commit properties on an idempotent replay (or record their completion atomically with the revision) and route them through the marker check.
